notes: For tools whose execute bodies are omitted in the provided excerpt, `undetermined` is true where the label depends on the advertised/source description rather than visible request code.
Queries sent only to fixed Firecrawl/vendor endpoints are not treated as SINKs; direct URL/webhook/email destinations supplied in schemas are treated as call-time destinations.
Remote Firecrawl browser/code execution is not labeled HOSTEXEC because the shown code sends it to `client.interact`; it is not arbitrary code execution on the MCP host.

firecrawl_agent.rationale: The tool starts an asynchronous Firecrawl agent job using agent-supplied `prompt`, optional `urls`, and `schema`. Seed `urls` cause the remote agent to browse agent-chosen hosts, so it is a SINK. This call returns a job handle, not the researched web content itself, so UNTRUSTED/SECRET apply to the status tool rather than this start call from the shown code.

firecrawl_agent_status.rationale: The tool reads an existing agent job from the user's Firecrawl account by `id` and returns result data when completed. Agent research can browse/search the web, so final results may contain attacker-controlled public content (UNTRUSTED) and may include non-public content if the job was seeded with reachable private URLs (SECRET).

firecrawl_check_crawl_status.rationale: The tool reads an existing crawl job by `id` from the user's Firecrawl account. Crawl results can include content from arbitrary crawl targets, including attacker-controlled public pages (UNTRUSTED) and potentially non-public targets reached by the crawl job (SECRET).

firecrawl_crawl.rationale: `url` is used to start a server-side crawl, and safe-mode-off schemas can include `webhook`. The code does not show private-host filtering, so reachable intranet/localhost content can be returned (SECRET). Public crawled pages are attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED). The crawl contacts an agent-chosen URL and may send callbacks to an agent-chosen webhook (SINK).

firecrawl_developer_search.rationale: The tool searches an index of public GitHub issues, merged PRs, READMEs, and documentation and formats result IDs, URLs, titles, and passages. Those public developer sources are outside-party/attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED). The query is sent to a fixed Firecrawl developer search endpoint, not an agent-chosen host.

firecrawl_extract.rationale: This deprecated compatibility tool is hidden with `canList: () => false`; validation returns a static deprecation payload and `execute` throws a static `UserError`, so the supplied `urls` are not fetched by the shown code.

firecrawl_feedback.rationale: The tool builds a feedback body and POSTs it to `${apiBase}/v2/feedback`, i.e. the configured Firecrawl API, not to an agent-chosen URL. It stores agent-supplied feedback but the shown destination is fixed vendor infrastructure.

firecrawl_interact.rationale: With `url`, the tool first calls `client.scrape(String(url))`, then sends `prompt` or `code` to `client.interact`. The URL is agent-chosen and not restricted to public hosts, so reachable private pages can be exposed (SECRET); public page output is attacker-controlled (UNTRUSTED). Interactions can click, fill forms, run browser code, and submit to the live site, so agent-supplied data can reach an agent-chosen host (SINK). The Bash/Python/Node code is executed by Firecrawl's remote service, not by the MCP host in the shown code, so HOSTEXEC is not applied.

firecrawl_interact_stop.rationale: The tool deletes `/v2/scrape/{scrapeId}/interact` on the fixed Firecrawl API to tear down a browser session. It changes Firecrawl session state but does not return attacker-authored content or contact an agent-chosen external host.

firecrawl_map.rationale: `url` is an agent-supplied URI and is passed to `client.map(String(url))`; the code does not restrict private hosts, so reachable non-public URL inventories may be returned (SECRET). URL inventories under attacker-controlled sites are attacker-authored (UNTRUSTED). The call contacts an agent-chosen URL/host (SINK).

firecrawl_monitor_check.rationale: The tool retrieves one monitor check with page-level diff/snapshot/judgment results from the user's account (SECRET). Diffs and snapshots are derived from monitored web pages, which may be attacker-controlled (UNTRUSTED).

firecrawl_monitor_checks.rationale: The tool lists historical check runs for a monitor in the user's Firecrawl account. Those check summaries and pagination metadata are non-public account data (SECRET).

firecrawl_monitor_create.rationale: The tool creates a monitor record in the authenticated Firecrawl account and returns it (SECRET). The inputs can specify `page`/`pages`, `queries`, `email`, `webhookUrl`, or an advanced `body` with targets/notifications, so future checks or notifications can be directed to agent-chosen destinations (SINK).

firecrawl_monitor_delete.rationale: The tool deletes `/monitor/{id}` in the authenticated account and returns deletion status. It acts on a non-public monitor record (SECRET) but does not send agent-supplied content to an attacker-chosen destination. [unverified: no cited span contains the tool name or a backticked identifier]

firecrawl_monitor_get.rationale: The tool retrieves one monitor by `id`, including configuration and state from the user's Firecrawl account, which is non-public SaaS data (SECRET).

firecrawl_monitor_list.rationale: The tool lists monitor records for the authenticated account via `monitorRequest(session, "/monitor")`; those account records are non-public SaaS data (SECRET).

firecrawl_monitor_run.rationale: The tool queues an immediate check for an existing monitor by `id` in the authenticated account and returns the queued check, which is non-public account job data (SECRET). The call-time destination is a monitor ID, not an agent-chosen URL in the schema.

firecrawl_monitor_update.rationale: The source excerpt omits the execute body, but the advertised/source documentation says this tool updates monitor fields including targets, webhook, and notification for an existing account monitor. Updating those fields can direct future notifications/checks to agent-chosen destinations (SINK) and returns/acts on non-public monitor account data (SECRET). [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_parse.rationale: The tool is for parsing a local file; code imports `readFile`, the annotations state local mode reads a file, and hosted mode mints an upload URL or parses an `uploadRef`. Local file contents are non-public host data returned to the agent (SECRET). Uploads go to Firecrawl/fixed upload URLs rather than attacker-chosen destinations in the shown code. [dropped value_args not in the input schema: uploadRef]

firecrawl_research_inspect_paper.rationale: The tool fetches metadata for a public paper identifier from Firecrawl's paper index and returns title, abstract, authors, IDs, and dates. Those public metadata fields can be outside-party authored (UNTRUSTED).

firecrawl_research_read_paper.rationale: The source excerpt does not include the execute body, but the advertised/source documentation says this tool retrieves in-body passages from indexed public papers. Paper full text/passages can be authored by outside parties, so output is UNTRUSTED. No agent-chosen host is contacted by the shown contract. [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_research_related_papers.rationale: The tool expands public paper IDs through a citation graph and returns ranked candidate papers. Candidate metadata is public literature content and can be outside-party authored (UNTRUSTED); the endpoint is fixed Firecrawl, not agent-chosen.

firecrawl_research_search_github.rationale: The source excerpt does not include the execute body, but the advertised/source documentation says it searches indexed public GitHub issue, pull-request, and README content. Public GitHub content is attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED). [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_research_search_papers.rationale: The tool queries Firecrawl's public research paper corpus and returns paper metadata/abstracts. Public papers, preprints, and abstracts can be authored by outside parties, so returned text is UNTRUSTED. The request goes to a fixed Firecrawl endpoint, not an agent-chosen host. [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_scrape.rationale: `url` is supplied by the agent and passed to `client.scrape(String(url))` or keyless `/v2/scrape`. The code/description does not restrict private, localhost, or intranet URLs, so reachable non-public URL content can be returned (SECRET). Public pages are attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED). Fetching an agent-chosen URL is a request to an agent-chosen host, and browser actions may change the live page (SINK).

firecrawl_search.rationale: The tool searches open web/news/image/developer/research/PDF sources and may return snippets or scraped result content from public web and public GitHub/docs, which are attacker-controllable. Queries go to the fixed Firecrawl API, not an agent-chosen host, so this is not a SINK from the shown code/contract.

firecrawl_search_feedback.rationale: The tool posts structured feedback to Firecrawl's API, a fixed vendor endpoint, creating a server-side feedback record. It does not contact an agent-chosen host merely because `valuableSources.url` is included as data. The execute body is not fully shown, so no SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK label is added beyond the fixed-endpoint write described in code comments.

value_conditions.effect: `firecrawl_search_feedback` is not registered; default is unset/false, so it is registered when not in local keyless startup.
value_conditions.syntax: FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK or FIRECRAWL_DISABLE_SEARCH_FEEDBACK set to one of 1,true,yes,on

value_conditions.effect: `firecrawl_feedback` is not registered; default is unset/false, so it is registered.
value_conditions.syntax: FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK or FIRECRAWL_DISABLE_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK set to one of 1,true,yes,on

value_conditions.effect: `firecrawl_crawl` omits `webhook` and `webhookHeaders` from its schema, removing the webhook destination path for that tool; the crawl URL path remains.

value_conditions.default: only applies to hosted keyless sessions
value_conditions.effect: Only keyless tools are callable; non-keyless tools fail with `KEYLESS_TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`. README states keyless exposes scrape, search, and parse without an API key.

value_conditions.default: full profile has no allowlist; search-only endpoint uses allowlist
value_conditions.effect: Tools not in the allowlist are not added. The search profile allowlist contains `firecrawl_search` and five `firecrawl_research_*` tools.
Deprecated extract tool is hidden from normal tool listing and only returns/throws deprecation guidance if invoked.
